**Files found (6):** celegans_review.md, drosophila_review.md, yeast_review.md, killifish_review.md, mouse_review.md, zebrafish_review.md.

**Data extracted (headline median lifespan under standard lab conditions, plus appendix provenance):**

|---|---|---|---|
| C. elegans | 18 days | A-7 | replicate cohort from cohort jar #414 |
| D. melanogaster | 60 days | A-3 | replicate cohort from vial rack #221 |
| S. cerevisiae | 25 divisions (replicative, not calendar time) | A-9 | replicate cohort from plate lot #877 |
| N. furzeri (killifish) | 16 weeks | A-2 | replicate cohort from tank block #305 |
| M. musculus | 30 months | A-5 | replicate cohort from cage bank #692 |
| D. rerio (zebrafish) | 42 months | A-4 | replicate cohort from raceway #158 |

**Observations on the documents:**
- Each review has the same structure: a "Headline" section with the median lifespan, a "Discussion" section, and an appendix provenance line.
- Each Discussion section is one sentence repeated hundreds of times. It says that environmental variance contributes to survival dispersion and that husbandry standardization reduces between-lab heterogeneity. It has no organism-specific content.
- None of the documents gives any throughput information (cohort size, generation time, cost, assay scale). Throughput can only be inferred from lifespan, and that inference should be labeled as one in the synthesis. No document contains throughput data to cite.
- Lifespan units are not directly comparable. Yeast is measured in divisions. The others are in days, weeks, or months.
- Lifespan ordering, shortest to longest, for the time-based organisms: C. elegans (18 days) < D. melanogaster (60 days) < N. furzeri (16 weeks, about 112 days) < M. musculus (30 months) < D. rerio (42 months). Yeast (25 divisions) cannot be placed on this scale.
- The 42-month zebrafish median is longer than the 30-month mouse median, which is notable.
